items.title: Orion's brain is running
items.detail: Checks that Orion's brain answers.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Orion's key works
items.detail: Checks that local tools can read Orion's key and that Orion accepts it.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: The Orion window is connected
items.detail: Checks that this window talks to Orion's brain.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.
items.watch: Ticks itself when the Orion window connects.

items.title: Health light is green
items.detail: Checks Orion's health light (green or amber is fine).
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Every part started
items.detail: Checks that no part of Orion was switched off because it failed.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: The black hole draws and picks a quality
items.detail: The Orion window checks that the black hole can draw and which quality it picked.
items.next: Tap Do it for me.

items.title: Windows look like frosted glass
items.detail: Orion's windows should be see-through glass with the black hole glowing behind them.
items.next: Tap Do it for me, look at this window, and answer the question.

items.title: Orion hears a microphone
items.detail: Checks that Orion's voice typing is running with a microphone.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Orion speaks out loud
items.detail: Orion says one sentence out of your speakers.
items.next: Turn your sound up and tap Do it for me. Orion speaks, then asks if you heard it.

items.title: Hot mic and wake word are off by default
items.detail: Checks that Orion doesn't listen all the time unless you turn it on.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Your phone is paired
items.detail: Checks that a phone is paired with this PC.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.
items.watch: Ticks itself as soon as your phone is paired.

items.title: Your phone reaches this PC
items.detail: Checks that your phone talked to this PC in the last 15 minutes.
items.next: Open Orion Mobile on your phone, then tap Run all automatic checks.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone talks to this PC.

items.title: The phone's fingerprint key is ready
items.detail: Your phone checks this itself: the approval key is in its secure chip and needs your fingerprint.
items.next: On your phone, open Orion Mobile > Menu > Test. It fills this in by itself.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone runs its own test (Orion Mobile > Menu > Test).

items.title: The phone can read message notifications
items.detail: Needed for the one inbox. Your phone checks this itself.
items.next: On your phone, open Orion Mobile > Menu > Test and tap Do it for me: it opens the right page.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone runs its own test (Orion Mobile > Menu > Test).

items.title: Long-press power opens Orion
items.detail: Orion is the phone's assistant app. Your phone checks this itself.
items.next: On your phone, open Orion Mobile > Menu > Test and tap Do it for me: it opens the right page.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone runs its own test (Orion Mobile > Menu > Test).

items.title: The phone won't put Orion to sleep
items.detail: Battery saving is off for Orion, so alerts arrive on time. Your phone checks this itself.
items.next: On your phone, open Orion Mobile > Menu > Test and tap Do it for me: it opens the right page.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone runs its own test (Orion Mobile > Menu > Test).

items.title: Approve a test card with your fingerprint
items.detail: Orion sends a test card that does nothing. You approve it on your phone with your fingerprint.
items.next: Tap Do it for me, then approve the card on your phone with your fingerprint.
items.watch: Ticks itself when you approve (or reject) the card on your phone. Orion never approves it.

items.title: Drafts are never sent by the PC
items.detail: Makes a test reply draft and checks that nothing is sent.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Draft a reply on your phone
items.detail: On the phone, a draft appears in your style and nothing is sent until you tap Send yourself.
items.next: On your phone, open a message in Orion's inbox, tap Draft, then close it without sending.
items.watch: Ticks itself when your phone asks this PC for a draft.

items.title: Send work to the PC
items.detail: From the phone, queue a small mission for the PC's agents.
items.next: On your phone, open Missions and send "Test mission" to your PC.
items.watch: Ticks itself when a mission from your phone reaches this PC.

items.title: Pocket Orion answers when the PC is off
items.detail: Only if you set up Pocket Orion: the phone keeps working without the PC.
items.next: Quit Orion on the PC, ask Orion Mobile something, and tap Done if Pocket Orion answers (your phone skips this by itself if Pocket Orion isn't set up).

items.title: Coding agents are found
items.detail: Looks for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI on this PC.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: A practice mission makes a review card
items.detail: A stand-in agent edits a scratch repo in a temporary folder; Orion checks it and makes a review card. Nothing is approved and everything is deleted afterwards.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: A real mission with Claude Code
items.detail: A small real mission with Claude Code on a test repo, from start to review card. It may cost a few cents. Merging stays your choice.
items.next: Tap Do it for me to start "Add a hello file" with Claude Code on a test repo.
items.watch: Ticks itself when the review card arrives.

items.title: Start a project with Claude
items.detail: Starting a project makes the project and its first mission.
items.next: Tap Do it for me: Projects opens with a sample idea filled in. Press Start there.
items.watch: Ticks itself when the project's first mission reaches review.

items.title: Record a tiny skill
items.detail: Orion watches you do 3 small steps once on a practice page that only lives on this computer.
items.next: Tap Do it for me: a practice page opens and Orion starts recording. Do its 3 steps, then press Save on the skill card.
items.watch: Ticks itself when the skill is saved.

items.title: Replay the skill
items.detail: Orion repeats what you recorded.
items.next: Tap Do it for me: Orion replays the practice skill on the practice page.
items.watch: Ticks itself when the replay gets to the end.

items.title: Freeze Orion from your phone
items.detail: The kill switch: everything that changes Orion stops.
items.next: On your phone, tap Freeze and confirm with your fingerprint.
items.watch: Ticks itself when Orion is frozen from your phone.

items.title: Unfreeze from your phone
items.detail: Only your fingerprint lets Orion run again.
items.next: On your phone, tap Unfreeze and approve it with your fingerprint.
items.watch: Ticks itself when Orion runs again after your approval.

items.title: Undo the last change
items.detail: Orion can always go back to how it was before its last change.
items.next: After the screen change test, approve the practice change if you like, then tap Do it for me to put it back.
items.watch: Ticks itself when a change is undone.

items.title: The privacy dashboard turns everything off
items.detail: One button turns off everything Orion can see or hear.
items.next: Tap Do it for me: Orion presses Turn everything off and reads every switch back.

items.title: A small screen change shows a preview first
items.detail: Orion builds a practice change (it only recolours a practice banner) in a separate copy and shows a ghost preview before anything changes. The Test Center never applies it.
items.next: Tap Do it for me and wait for the ghost preview in the corner (a minute or two).
items.watch: Ticks itself when the ghost preview is ready.

items.title: Wi-Fi is connected
items.detail: Checks that the computer is on a network.
items.next: Tap Run all automatic checks.

items.title: Sleep and lock work
items.detail: Only on real hardware: closing the lid sleeps and locks; opening it asks for your password.
items.next: Tap Do it for me, close the lid for ten seconds, and open it.
items.watch: Notices the sleep by itself, then asks if it locked.

items.title: Restart into Windows
items.detail: Windows starts once; next time OrionOS is the normal choice again.
items.next: Open the app menu, pick Restart into Windows, and tap Done when you're back in Orion.

privacy.label: Screen reading
privacy.what: Reads the text on your screen, on this computer, so Orion can help with what you're doing. Password managers, banking and private windows are always skipped.
privacy.how_on: Settings > Privacy > Orion reads your screen

privacy.label: Tips from what's on screen
privacy.what: Suggests things based on the window you're in.

privacy.label: Guide Mode
privacy.what: Looks at the screen only while it walks you through a task, to put the ring on the next button.

privacy.label: Hot mic
privacy.what: Listens for your voice all the time and only acts on you saying “Orion, …”. Nothing is recorded or saved. Ctrl+Alt+M mutes it.

privacy.label: Wake word “Orion”
privacy.what: A small model on this computer listens for the word “Orion” before anything else is checked.

privacy.label: Voice typing
privacy.what: Turns speech into text on this computer while Orion's window is in use.

privacy.label: Camera and presence
privacy.what: The camera itself. Orion doesn't watch for you with it; this switch stops every app from opening it.

privacy.label: Recorders
privacy.what: Watch-and-learn recording of clicks and typing, and browser skill recording. Only between your start and stop.

privacy.label: Inbox mirror
privacy.what: Copies your phone's messages to this computer so Orion can draft replies. Never sends anything.
privacy.how_on: Settings > Orion > Mirror inbox to my PC

privacy.label: Usage data
privacy.what: Orion sends no usage data anywhere. There is nothing to turn on.

privacy.label: Crash reports
privacy.what: None are sent. Crashes are fixed on this computer by the crash fixer, which only proposes fixes.

starters.run: Open index.html in a browser (or press Play it in Orion). Tests: node --test

starters.description: A simple website: a page, a stylesheet and a little script.

starters.label: Python tool
starters.description: A small command-line tool in Python, with a test.

starters.label: Empty

starters.run: Whatever Claude builds; the README will say.

templates.label: New website
templates.title: New website
templates.description: Build a small, fast website in a new folder. Pages: home, about, contact. Plain HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript; no paid services or trackers. Add a README saying how to open it.

templates.label: New game prototype
templates.title: New game prototype
templates.description: Make a small playable game prototype in a new folder: one level, simple controls, a win and a lose state. Use only free assets you draw in code. Add a README with how to run it.
